messages:
kyle: Noticing a different nvme problem in eu-west3: thermal throttling spikes coinciding with a sudden write-amplification window. GPUs are waiting on attach for longer than usual (~2x), and a few preemptible attaches timed out.
maria: Any clue what's causing the write-amplification? background jobs? snapshot churn?
kyle: Looks like a bulk image conversion job from a customer hit the cohort and kicked off many small writes; combined with an aggressive scrub on some nodes we get tail write storms. Example log from gn-eu3-151: `nvme0: write latency tail 450ms, thermal_throttle=1, write_amp=4.2x`.
raj: Oof. That smells like tiny-IO-heavy workload + overlayfs metadata pressure. Options: 1) absorb by shifting attaches to dedicated pool, 2) throttle the background job at the job scheduler, 3) set janitor ratecap for affected cohort.
ana: I'd prefer a three-step mitigation: immediate throttle janitor and mark nodes avoid:new-attach, short-term reroute attaches, and ask customer to rate-limit their job (we can enforce via tenant QoS if needed).
leo: Quick commands I ran: `opsctl tag gn-eu3-149 nvme:thermal_hot=true` and `opsctl route-add temporary eu-west3:attach -> eu-west3-dedicated-2 priority=high duration=15m`. Also set janitor cap: `curl -s -XPOST https://ops-api.internal/v1/janitor/ratecap -d '{"cohort":"scratch-cohort-11","iops_cap":25000,"duration":"20m"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'`
infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_thermal_throttle_detected on scratch-cohort-11 (gn-eu3-148..gn-eu3-153). Attaches delayed: 9 in last 12m.
ops-sre: Approving temporary route and janitor cap. Log: `incident:1747001234 mitigation:janitor_ratecap(25k), route_to_dedicated(15m), tags_applied`.
maria: After applying caps+route, attach lat p95 dropped from 1.1s -> 420ms over 8m. Good recovery.
raj: Cost note: routing to dedicated pool increases per-attach cost; estimate marginal +$900/day if maintained for 24h. Let's keep window short and try scheduling the customer's batch for off-peak.
kyle: Next steps: 1) Ops to keep janitor cap for 20m and observe, 2) SRE to notify customer to slow job, 3) Schedule firmware update for that NVMe cohort next maintenance (non-urgent) if SMART shows rising temp cycles. I'll open a follow-up ticket with SMART trend and telemetry.
ops-sre: Creating ticket INF-2026-1747 with telemetry attached. If thermal cycles > threshold we'll trigger proactive replacement.
leo: Quick note: we'll also add a short-lived metric-alert to reduce MTTR if this pattern repeats: `nvme.write_amp > 3 for 5m` -> page oncall.
kyle: TL;DR: thermal write-amplification from customer job + scrub caused NVMe thermal throttle and attach delays. Throttled janitor, tagged hot nodes, routed new attaches to dedicated pool, informed customer. Monitoring. :white_check_mark:
